summary: CLI exposes installer host to remote shell execution and interactive PTY driven by api.ai-support-agent.com
details: Once started via its bin/service entry, the CLI registers as a long-running agent to api.ai-support-agent.com, subscribes to AppSync notifications, and executes 'agent_command' payloads received from that remote server. The shell-executor path feeds a server-supplied command directly into spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command]) with the installer's privileges. A parallel WebSocket channel (/ws/agent-terminal) decodes base64 'stdin' frames from the server and writes them into a real bash/zsh PTY via node-pty/tmux (dist/vscode/vscode-server.js, dist/browser/browser-local-server.js, dist/api-client.js). The service-install path (dist/cli/service/darwin-service.js, dist/cli/service/linux-service.js) registers the agent as a launchd/systemd service with PATH modifications so the remote-controlled shell survives reboots. The result is that whoever controls api.ai-support-agent.com holds an interactive shell and full-host RCE on the installer's machine for as long as the service is enabled. This is the package's advertised purpose (a remote AI support agent), but by shape it is a first-party vendor-operated backdoor: trust in the CLI is equivalent to granting persistent shell access to the operator of that SaaS.
